newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan concerned Israel proceeded with building plan.
newsitem.headline: Annan concerned Israel proceeded with building plan.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan expressed "disappointment and deep concern" on Tuesday that Israel had decided to proceed with a controversial building project in Arab East Jerusalem, despite international appeals not to do so.
"He calls on the parties to do their utmost to find mutually acceptable solutions and proceed with the peace negotiations," a statement issued through a U.N. spokesman said.

"The secretary-general has learned with disappointment and deep concern that, despite international appeals, the Israeli authorities have decided to proceed with construction at Jabal Abu Ghneim/Har Homa," the statement said.

Israel began work on Tuesday on building the first of a planned 6,500 homes for Jews on a pine-covered hill, called Jabal Abu Ghneim by Palestinians and Har Homa by Israelis. The site, between Jerusalem and Bethlehem, was captured by Israel during the 1967 Midle East war.

The U.N. General Assembly adopted a resolution last Thursday, by a vote of 130 to two with two abstentions, calling on Israel to abandon plans for the project. Only Israel and the United States voted against the resolution.
The Assembly acted after the United States vetoed a similar resolution in the Security Council on March 7.

The United States joined virtually all other speakers in both the Assembly and Security Council debates in oppossing the Israeli action. But it said the United Nations was not the appropriate forum for dealing with issues that should be settled directly between Israel and the Palestinians.
